ind.1.1: Customer evidence in board and management attention
ind.5.4: Response to pressure: build or retrench

read: This assessment applies Jeff Bezos's Day 1 / Day 2 lens to a listed company's board, using public information only. Day 1 boards stay obsessed with the customer, make high-velocity decisions, resist proxies and process, embrace external trends, build rather than protect, and manage to cash. Day 2 is what creeps in afterwards.

Six dimensions, 22 indicators. Each indicator is scored 1 (Day 2), 3 (Mixed) or 5 (Day 1) against written anchors, once, for the board. Management's observable actions are attributed to the board's oversight, because a listed board is accountable for what the company does under its watch. Scores of 2 and 4 are used only where evidence meets parts of both adjacent anchors.

Overall grades are the rounded average of the dimension letters (A=5 … F=1; midpoints round down, so 2.5 is a D); provisional where only three dimensions are reported. Where evidence falls below the minimum, an indicator is marked not assessable and excluded rather than scored as Mixed, with the cause recorded (disclosure-limited, retrieval-limited, rule-limited). Peers are assessed on public information only.
method: 01  Every indicator is scored once, for the board; a cell with nothing to assess is marked not applicable.
02  Scores are 1, 3 or 5; 2 and 4 only where evidence meets parts of both adjacent anchors.
03  A 1 or 5 requires two independent items from two documents, or one strong direct item (regulator or court record, formal board act, audited figure, or a board document); a 3 requires one.

04  Confidence is assigned on the evidence: High = two direct sources or one strong source; Medium = one direct or two indirect; Low = a single indirect source, an inference, a silence-based score, or self-assessment alone.

05  Below the minimum an indicator is not assessable and excluded, never defaulted to 3; silence is scorable in full on 1.4, 5.2, 5.3 and capped at 3 on 2.3, 2.4, 4.3; an empty register search supports up to 3 on 1.3.
06  A dimension grade is reported only if at least half (outside-in) or two-thirds (post inside-out) of its indicators are assessed.
07  Overall grade is the rounded average of dimension letters, with midpoints rounding down (for example, an average of 2.5 is a D); provisional at three dimensions; none below three.
08  Behaviour indicators use 24 months (36 for 2.1 and 4.3); trend indicators five years of filings.
09  3.2, 5.1, 6.1 and 6.2 are scored relative to the named peer set.
10  Within scoped pairs an evidence item is primary for one indicator only.
11  Approved news and trade press (for event facts) are direct evidence; formal board acts are strong direct evidence.

12  Inside-out: board documents outrank public sources; the post inside-out score must cite at least one inside-out or self-assessment item; self-assessment alone is at most Medium confidence; peers are never re-scored.
13  Each company is run twice on the same rule version; indicator scores within one point and unchanged dimension letters are required for the result to stand.
docs: Governance framework: delegation of authority, committee terms, capital and treasury policies, incentive scorecards
Capital and investment papers with post-investment reviews
Treasury and liquidity reports (stress tests, covenant headroom)
Board evaluation report and action log
Skills matrix and board/CEO succession plans
Chair / lead independent director notes from executive sessions
q: Customer Obsession

In the last 12 months, when did something a customer said or did change a decision in the boardroom? How did it reach you: through management's summary, or directly (complaints, churn data, a conversation without management present)?
Customer Obsession
Which customer or quality measure sits in executive pay, at what weight, and has it ever reduced a payout?
Resisting Proxies
When did the board last change a core strategic assumption, and what prompted it: internal evidence the board asked for, or outside pressure (a miss, an activist, an analyst)?
Resisting Proxies
Which number in the board pack do you trust least, and what has the board retired or redefined in the last two years (a metric, a report, a committee) because it no longer earned its place?
Embracing External Trends

Name the two or three structural shifts that matter most to the company. For each, does the board hold an explicit position with targets, and who outside the company has addressed the board on it in the past year?
Embracing External Trends
On the last two or three sector shocks, did the company move ahead of peers, with them, or after them, and did the board or management initiate the move?
High-Velocity Decision-Making

Does the board distinguish reversible from irreversible decisions in practice? Give one example of each from the last year, how many meetings each took, and whether anything was reversed, deferred or declined.
High-Velocity Decision-Making
When did a director last change their mind because of an argument made in the room, how are minority views recorded, and does a contested decision stay settled afterwards?
Building over Protecting
When earnings last came under pressure, which lever did the board reach for first (cost, buybacks, guidance, reinvestment), and how was the alternative debated?
Building over Protecting
What did the last board evaluation and the last board appointment change, and what would owners say about the board that the board would not say about itself?
Liquidity and Capital Management
Does the board spend more time on earnings or on cash? What liquidity trigger would make the board act, and has it ever acted while the numbers still looked fine?
Liquidity and Capital Management
What is the stated leverage and liquidity policy, how often is it stress-tested in front of the board, and who on the board owns working capital?

anchors11.1: Customer appears only as revenue or market share inside financial reporting and messaging.
anchors11.3: Periodic customer reviews based on management-curated metrics (e.g., NPS, retention), selectively surfaced.
anchors11.5: Customer outcomes are a standing priority; unfiltered evidence (complaints, churn drivers, lost deals) is routinely examined and openly acknowledged.
